column1: # Registry spellings that no string transform can reach, mapped to Oncotree
# display names. Tab-delimited: alias, Oncotree display name, why.
# This table is ONLY for the cases utils/reference_validation._fold cannot
# handle. Folding already forgives case, apostrophes, hyphens, slashes and
# British spelling, so "Wilms Tumor" -> "Wilms' Tumor" and "High Grade
# Glioma, NOS" -> "High-Grade Glioma, NOS" need no entry here and must not
# get one. What is left is three kinds of genuine mismatch:
#   1. Granularity. Oncotree splits what a registry does not. "Acute
#      Lymphoblastic Leukemia" names no lineage; Oncotree has only B- and
#      T-lineage nodes, so a lineage has to be chosen. That is a clinical
#      decision, not a naming fact, which is why it is written down here
#      where a clinician can disagree with it rather than buried in code.
#   2. Reclassification. WHO CNS5 retired Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma;
#      our Oncotree carries the successor. MeSH still lists DIPG as current,
#      so no external synonym source bridges this - only a dated decision.
#   3. Registry house style. NCI/COG trials write "Stage II Kidney Wilms
#      Tumor"; the organ is part of the label, not a qualifier.
# Aliases are applied AFTER an exact, code, case- and fold-insensitive lookup
# has failed, so nothing here can shadow a real Oncotree name. An alias whose
# own name already resolves is rejected at load time as dead weight.
# Deliberately absent: the bare string "ALL". Three-character aliases are how
# the gene table went wrong (see the module docstring in
# utils/reference_validation), and a condition list that says only "ALL" is
# rare enough to be worth a review queue rather than a guess.
# alias
Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
column3: Oncotree splits lineage, registries do not; paediatric ALL is B-lineage in ~85% of cases
